problem: 'a face turned away from the camera gives the opposite sign at the eye' is elliptical. It never says that the plane expression must be evaluated at the eye point, and 'opposite sign' does not say opposite to what. A student can easily invert the test and cull the front faces instead of the back faces.
fix: Write the test out: with outward normals, substitute the eye point E = (Ex, Ey, Ez) into the left side to get f(E) = A·Ex + B·Ey + C·Ez + D. If f(E) > 0 the eye is on the normal side, so the face points toward the camera and is drawn; if f(E) < 0 the face points away and can be culled. Also state the convention that vertices are listed counter-clockwise when seen from outside, so that (P2 − P1) × (P3 − P1) is the outward normal.

problem: The plane constant is the capital D, and the signed distance is introduced as lowercase d. Two symbols that differ only in case, in the same paragraph, invite copying errors in the exam.
fix: Call the signed distance something distinct, for example write: the true signed distance is (A·x + B·y + C·z + D)/|n|, or name it d_perp.

problem: 'Quoting an unnormalised normal as though its length were a distance' is confusing: the length of the normal is never the distance. The real mistake is treating the raw value Ax + By + Cz + D, which is |n| times the distance, as a distance in model units.
fix: Reword as: 'Reporting Ax + By + Cz + D as a distance. It equals |n| times the signed distance, so it is only a distance after division by |n|.'

problem: 'Only a few universities teach the coefficient formulas; most courses use the plane only for the back-face test' is unclear and contradicts the chapter itself, which does derive A, B, C, D and uses them for more than back-face removal. 'Coefficient formulas' is undefined.
fix: Either delete the sentence or replace it with a plain statement, for example: 'The same plane equation is reused later for clipping and for BSP splitting, so keep A, B, C, D rather than only the cross product.'

problem: The lead promises that the equation gives 'the distance from the origin', but the text only gives the signed distance of a general point P. The distance from the origin, |D|/|n|, is never shown.
fix: Add after the unit-normal line: 'At the origin the value is D, so the perpendicular distance from the origin to the plane is |D|/|n|.'

problem: The answer 'outside the solid' is only guaranteed for a convex solid. For a concave solid, a point on the outward side of one face plane can still sit inside another part of the same solid.
fix: Answer: 'The point is on the camera side of that face plane, so it is outside the half-space bounded by the face; for a convex solid this means outside the solid. The 5 is |n| times the distance, not 5 units.'
